Draft1 will distinguish semantic staging from physical boundedness and define the remediation/conformance plan.

title: Information gathering & display
description:
Surface the metadata, timeline, and lineage around opencode sessions so a user can orient on *what a session is and how it came to be* — not just whether it matches a search term.

Today `cotails` reports only `id`, `slug`, `title`, `updated`, and a text `snippet`. The opencode schema carries far richer signal that is currently invisible (all on the `session` table unless noted):

- **Provenance:** `time_created` (when it began), `directory` / `path` (where), `project_id` -> `project.name`.
- **Fork lineage:** `fork_session_id` + `fork_message_id` — the parent session and the exact message at which this session diverged.
- **Lifecycle:** `time_compacting`, `time_suspended`, `time_archived`.
- **Cost/usage:** `cost`, `tokens_input`, `tokens_output`, `tokens_reasoning`, `tokens_cache_read`/`write`.

This epic owns **reporting** — reading these fields and rendering them in both human and `--json` output. It does NOT own the matching/query side (search & scoping epic) or the FTS index (index epic).

## Scope (children)
- `cotail-created-at` — first `time_created`.
- `cotail-fork-time` — last fork time.
- `cotail-fork-point` — the previous prompt+reply and fork prompt+reply around the fork boundary, with timestamps.
- `cotail-directory` — the session directory (implement first).

## Out of scope
- Search semantics, scoping filters, FTS index, Rust port (separate epics).

title: End Session: explicit closure reports and reusable handoffs
description:
# End Session

Make the end of an OpenCode work session an explicit, useful boundary rather than an ambiguous final chat message. A user can say or invoke **end session** to ask the agent to reconcile what happened, close the work cleanly, and leave a durable reference for future threads.

Source idea log: [`opencode-patches.md`](file:///home/rektide/archive/doc/opencode-patches.md), entry **End Session**. This ticket is the reciprocal implementation/design reference from that log.

## Net behavior

The feature is intentionally a hybrid whose final packaging remains a design decision:

- A user-facing `end session` command or prompt starts closure.
- A reusable prompt/skill tells the agent to inspect the actual work and report back, not merely declare success.
- An OpenCode plugin tool supplies session identity and records or returns the closure reference.
- If the designed cotail bookmark capability is available in the future, save a completion bookmark and include its ID. Bookmark support currently exists as Beads work/designs, not as a command that can be assumed present.

## Closure report

The concluding report should state:

- Outcome and whether the intended work is actually complete.
- What was built or changed, with resolvable references to files, commits, tickets, designs, and other artifacts.
- What was verified and what was not.
- Loose cracks, accrued damage, unresolved decisions, and abandoned threads.
- Explicit handoffs and next actions, each with enough context to resume.
- Future ideas worth preserving without pretending they are committed work.
- Session references: the OpenCode session ID always; related or child sessions when relevant; a cotail bookmark ID when available.

The final output should include a compact reference block a future prompt can quote to mean “load/reference this session.” Outputs created from the session should be listed from the closure, and future tickets/docs/sessions should be able to link back to that stable reference.

## Guardrails

- Ending a session does not mean claiming success. It may explicitly close as complete, partial, blocked, or abandoned.
- Do not run automatically on every idle transition; closure is an intentional user boundary.
- Bookmark persistence is optional and capability-gated. Failure to bookmark must not lose the report or block closure.
- Do not conflate the raw session transcript, a handoff, a bookmark, and the closure report; define how they relate.

## Open design questions

- Is the best OpenCode surface a custom command, an agent-callable tool, a prompt/skill, or a thin composition of all three?
- Does the closure live only in the transcript, in bookmark `Intent`, or in a new structured closure artifact with relation edges?
- How should later artifacts create inbound backlinks to the closure/session?
- How should a future session resolve a quoted closure reference into selected context rather than blindly loading a whole transcript?

## Related cotail work

- Bookmark Pointer/Composite/Store designs under `.design/bookmarks/`.
- `cotail-read-session` for materializing transcript context.
- `cotail-cat-summarize` for generated session summaries.
- `cotail-session-report` for canonical session identity and metadata.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deliberate `end session` invocation produces one clear closure report and reusable reference block.
- The report distinguishes complete, partial, blocked, and abandoned outcomes and does not claim unverified success.
- Produced artifacts, related sessions, unresolved items, handoffs, and future ideas have explicit sections and resolvable identifiers or links where available.
- The OpenCode session ID is always present, so another thread can ask to reference the session even without bookmark support.
- Cotail bookmark integration is capability-gated, records the completion marker when available, and degrades cleanly when unavailable.
- The design explains how future sessions consume the reference and how artifacts created from a session link back to it.
- Tests cover activation, report/reference construction, absent bookmark capability, and nonfatal bookmark failure once an implementation shape is chosen.
notes: 2026-08-21: The bookmark redesign separates closure/handoff artifacts from Bookmark. End-session should compose cotail-session-report-capture and may create a bookmark as a nonfatal optional reference; it should not emit Pointer/Composite/save-point records.

title: Reverse file-use search: which sessions touched a path
description:
Inverse of cotail-fileuse-tool: given one or more target file/directory paths (or globs), list the **sessions** whose tool calls read and/or changed those paths. ## Why The forward search (cotail-fileuse-tool) starts from a session and shows the paths it touched. The common question is the other way around: "who read or edited this file / this directory?" — e.g. which sessions modified src/foo.ts, or which sessions touched anything under ~/src/compfuzor. Today there is no way to answer that without scanning every session by hand. ## Command shape (proposed) A new subcommand, working name `touched` (open naming decision): cotail touched [path|glob...] [--read] [--changed] [--directory

] [--since ] [--json] [--limit ] - Positional args are path/glob targets (AND semantics: a session matches if it touched ANY target by default; consider --all for AND-across-targets later). - `--read` — only Read/Glob/Grep tool accesses (default: read+changed). - `--changed` — only Edit/Write/Bash-mutating accesses (default: read+changed). - Default (no flag): both read and changed. - Reuse the scoping flags from search: --directory, --since, --limit, --json. ## Output Group by session: session id/title/directory/updated, plus the matched target paths and the tool op(s) that hit them (read vs changed, which tool). Reuse cotail-fileuse-tool's part reader (part.data $.$type='tool', args at $.state.input) and its out-of-project vs in-project distinction, but here the in-project paths are the interesting ones (target lives inside a session's own directory). ## Acceptance - `cotail touched ` lists sessions whose tool calls read or changed that path, newest first. - `--changed` and `--read` restrict to the respective tool categories. - Directory/glob targets work (e.g. `~/src/compfuzor/*.ts`). - Output shows the matched path(s) + tool op per session; --json emits JSONL. - Reuses the cotail-fileuse-tool part reader rather than reimplementing path extraction. ## Notes / open questions - Naming: `touched` vs `which` vs `who` vs `files` — confirm verb. - Shell-command path tokens are out of scope here (see cotail-fileuse-shell); this is tool-call only for v1. - Glob semantics: literal-realpath match vs glob. Prefer resolving realpaths and matching against globs, like cotail-fileuse-tool.
acceptance_criteria: cotail touched <path> returns sessions whose tool calls read/changed the path; --read/--changed filter the access type; directory & glob targets work; output shows matched path + tool op per session; reuses the cotail-fileuse-tool part reader; --json supported.

title: cat --summarize: summarize a session via an agent
description:
# `cat --summarize` — summarize a session via an agent

Adds a `--summarize` flag to `cotail cat` that runs the selected content slice
through an agent and prints a summary.

## Thesis (inherited from the `cotail-summarize` epic)

The `cat` selection flags ARE the summarization scope. `--summarize` collects
the same slice `cat` would display, then summarizes it:

- default scope (no selection flags) = **whole session including tool calls +
  reasoning** ("generally the whole thing, tool calls + thinking in all").
- any present `cat` flag narrows it, e.g.:
  - `cotail cat <sid> --summarize --final` — summarize only the closing exchange.
  - `cotail cat <sid> --summarize --head 5 --tool` — summarize the first 5 pairs incl. tool calls.
  - `cotail cat <sid> --summarize --since 2d --thinking` — summarize last 2 days incl. reasoning.

So `cat`'s `--initial/--final/--head/--last/--thinking/--tool` (and the four
`--*-prompt/--*-response` halves) control both display and summarization — one
vocabulary.

## Agent transport (open question)

Invoke an agent to do the summarization. Candidate = **ACP (Agent Client
Protocol)**. Decide whether to call a local ACP/opencode endpoint or shell out
to a headless agent run. (Tracked on the parent epic.)

## CLI

```
cotail cat <sid> --summarize                     # whole session (text+tool+thinking)
cotail cat <sid> --summarize --final             # only the closing exchange
cotail cat <sid> --summarize --agent <name>      # choose summarizer agent
cotail cat <sid> --summarize --model <id>        # choose model
cotail cat <sid> --summarize --prompt <text>     # override the summary prompt
cotail cat <sid> --summarize --json              # { summary, params, ... }
cotail cat <sid> --summarize --no-cache          # bypass cotail-summary-cache
cotail cat <sid> --summarize --refresh           # force regenerate
```

## Parameter capture (feeds the cache)

Every summarization records: the selection scope (flags + range), a content
fingerprint of the selected slice, `agent`, `model`, and a `prompt_hash`. This
tuple is exactly what `cotail-summary-cache` keys on, so a cache hit =
"same session slice + same summarization config."

## Output

- default human — the summary text.
- `--json` — `{ summary, params: { scope, agent, model, promptHash, fingerprint, version } }`.

## Dependencies

- **Blocks on `cotail-read-session`** (the `cat` command) — it defines the selection flags this flag reuses.
- **Feeds `cotail-summary-cache`** — its parameter shape is the cache key.

## Acceptance

- `--summarize` produces a summary; default scope = whole session (text+tool+thinking).
- Every `cat` selection flag narrows the summarized scope.
- `--agent` / `--model` / `--prompt` selectable; agent transport implemented (ACP or decided alternative).
- `--json` emits summary + captured params; v1 + v2 readable.
acceptance_criteria: --summarize produces an agent summary; default scope = whole session (text+tool+thinking); every cat selection flag narrows scope; --agent/--model/--prompt selectable; --json emits summary+params; v1+v2.
notes: Repointed blocking dependency from the deleted cotail-cat to cotail-read-session (which is now the cat command).

title: Agent-generated session summaries
description:
# Agent-generated session summaries

Owns producing, displaying, and caching agent-generated summaries of sessions.

## Central thesis (from the originating discussion)

The content-selection flags defined on `cotail cat`
(`--initial/--final/--head/--last`, the four `--initial-prompt`/…/`--final-response`
halves, and `--thinking/--tool/--all`) are the **single vocabulary** used to
scope what gets summarized. `cotail cat <sid> --summarize` renders the selected
slice and hands it to an agent to summarize. Default summarization scope = the
whole session including tool calls + thinking ("generally the whole thing"),
but every `cat` flag narrows it. Display and summarization share one selection
model.

## Children

- `cotail-cat-summarize` — the `--summarize` flag on `cat`; produces a summary via an agent (candidate: ACP).
- `cotail-summary-cache` — a cotail-owned DB that persists summaries for reuse, capturing the summarization parameters.

## Open questions (tracked here)

- **Agent transport.** Candidate = **ACP (Agent Client Protocol)** — is there a
  local ACP/opencode endpoint to call, or do we shell out to a headless opencode
  run? Needs investigation; recorded so it isn't lost.

## Out of scope

- The FTS index (`cotail-index`), search/scoping (`cotail-search`), and
  write-side session mutation (`cotail-session-mgmt`).
acceptance_criteria: cat --summarize produces agent summaries scoped by cat's selection flags; summaries are cached for reuse with full parameter capture; agent transport (ACP candidate) decided and implemented.

title: search: --since recency filter
description:
Add a `--since <dur>` recency filter to `cotail search` that scopes results to sessions with `session.time_updated` after a cutoff, mirroring `cotail history --since`.

**Why.** `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on the current query shows `SCAN s` over all 3528 sessions with a per-session EXISTS regex subquery. `--since` compiles to a single `AND s.time_updated > ?` predicate in the outer WHERE, pruning sessions *before* the expensive `re()` evaluation — large speedup without needing the FTS index (`cotail-index`). Also answers "recent matches first / only recent" which the user keeps reaching for.

**Scope.** NOT currently in the `cotail-search` epic's listed scoping filters (`--directory`, `--session`, `--project`) — this ticket proposes adding temporal scoping as a peer. If accepted, the epic description should be updated to mention it.

**Implementation.**
- Site: `buildContentQuery` in [`src/opencode/source.ts`](src/opencode/source.ts). Add `sinceMs?: number` to `ContentQuery` (`src/opencode/types.ts`); when present, append `AND s.time_updated > ?` to the WHERE and push the param (epoch-ms).
- Lift `parseSince` (`src/commands/history.ts:24`) into shared code (`src/args.ts`) so `search` and `history` use the same parser. Existing grammar: `Nh`, `Nd`, `Nm`, ISO date; rejects with a helpful message.
- Plumb through `Args` + `parseArgs` in `src/commands/search.ts`; pass to `ContentQuery` as epoch-ms.
- Update `printHelp` and `README.md`'s search options block.

**Acceptance.**
- `cotail search foo --since 7d` returns only sessions updated in the last 7 days.
- `--since` accepts `24h`, `7d`, `30m`, and an ISO date; rejects garbage with the same error as `history`.
- `cotail search foo --since 7d` is observably faster than unscoped on a 3.5k-session DB.
- Shared parser used by both `search` and `history`.
notes:
Implemented in commit bf31fbb1.

Verified on the live 3.5k-session DB (today, 2026-08-05):
- `helpers --since 7d` → 0.89s (vs ~48s unscoped). 54x speedup, all hits confirmed Aug 3+.
- Grammar matches history: 24h/7d/30m and ISO dates accepted; bad input rejected with the same error.
- Combined with --directory works.
- parseSince lifted into src/args.ts; shared by search + history.

Implemented at the planned site (buildContentQuery + buildTitleQuery + ContentQuery.sinceMs).
2026-09-01: Search --since semantics changed from Session time_updated to Message time_created in commit 86244fac. Updated-time search continues in cotail-search-since-updated.
close_reason: Implemented in bf31fbb1. 54x speedup observed. parseSince shared with history via src/args.ts.

title: search: --directory filter
description:
Add a `--directory <path>` filter to `cotail search` that scopes results to sessions whose `session.directory` contains `<path>`, mirroring `cotail history --directory`.

**Why now.** `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on the current query shows `SCAN s` over all 3528 sessions, a per-session `SEARCH p EXISTS USING INDEX part_session_idx` (which still fires `json_extract` + the JS `re()` against every text part), and `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY` (no index on `session.time_updated`, so LIMIT can't short-circuit). `--directory` compiles to a single `s.directory LIKE '%' || ? || '%'` predicate added to the outer WHERE, pruning sessions *before* the EXISTS regex subquery runs — large speedup with no index.

**Scope.** Listed in `cotail-search` epic as a planned scoping filter. This ticket is the decomposition.

**Implementation.**
- Site: `buildContentQuery` in [`src/opencode/source.ts`](src/opencode/source.ts). Add optional `directory?: string` to `ContentQuery` (`src/opencode/types.ts`); when present, append `AND s.directory LIKE '%' || ? || '%'` to the WHERE and push the param.
- Lift `--directory` arg parsing out of `src/commands/history.ts` into shared code (e.g. `src/args.ts`) so `search` and `history` share one parser. History's docstring is "Only sessions whose directory contains <path>" — substring/contains, not exact. Keep that.
- Plumb through `Args` + `parseArgs` in `src/commands/search.ts`; pass to `ContentQuery`.
- Update `printHelp` and `README.md`'s search options block.

**Acceptance.**
- `cotail search foo --directory ~/src/compfuzor` returns only sessions with that path substring in `directory`.
- `--json`, `--title-only`, `--no-snippet` all still work with the new flag.
- `cotail search foo --directory <path>` is observably faster than unscoped on a 3.5k-session DB (EXISTS subquery runs against a strict subset of sessions).
- Shared parser used by both `search` and `history`.
notes:
Implemented in commit bf31fbb1.

Verified on the live 3.5k-session DB (today, 2026-08-05):
- `helpers --directory /home/rektide/src/compfuzor` → 3.04s (vs ~48s unscoped). 16x speedup, all hits confirmed compfuzor.
- Combined with --since works (`--title-only merge --directory compfuzor --since 14d` → 13 hits).
- Substring/contains semantics match history's docstring.
- parseSince lifted into src/args.ts; shared by search + history.

Followed the planned implementation site (buildContentQuery + buildTitleQuery + ContentQuery.directory).
close_reason: Implemented in bf31fbb1. 16x speedup observed. Both filters share the new src/args.ts parser with history.

title: find-id: return top N most recent matches
description:
# find-id with multiple results

`find-id` (and `get-session` before it) always returns a single session: `LIMIT 1` ordered by `time_updated DESC`. When you're not sure which session you want — "the last few sessions in this project", "what was I doing in compfuzor lately" — you need N results, not 1.

## CLI

- `--limit <n>` (default: `1`, current behavior).
- `--limit 0` = unlimited (mirrors `cotail history --limit`).

Today's `--id-only` and `--json` modes generalize naturally:

- `--id-only`: one id per line (scripting-friendly for loops).
- `--json`: one JSONL line per session (already works for one; emit N).
- default human: render as a small table (reuse `renderTable` from `src/format.ts`).

## Composition with cotail-find-id-cwd

That ticket resolves the directory from cwd; this ticket returns multiple. Combined: `cotail find-id --limit 5` from inside a project = "last 5 sessions here". They compose without coupling.

## Acceptance

- `cotail find-id --limit 5 [other args]` returns up to 5 sessions, most-recent-first.
- All three output modes (`--id-only`, `--json`, human table) work for N > 1.
- Default (`--limit 1`) preserves current single-session behavior exactly.
acceptance_criteria: find-id --limit N returns N sessions; --id-only/--json/table all handle N>1; default stays 1

title: Live session discovery via opencode HTTP server + mDNS
description:
# Discover the active opencode session over HTTP (with mDNS), not /proc heuristics

## Why

`cotail-get-session` (shipped) resolves an opencode PID → active session by
reading `/proc/<pid>/cwd` and matching the **most recently updated** session
in that directory. That works, but it is a heuristic: it can mis-pick when
several opencode instances share a directory, it cannot distinguish a busy
session from a merely-recent one, and it is Linux-only. opencode **already**
exposes precise live state over an HTTP server — we just have to turn it on
and point cotails at it.

## What opencode already supports (researched against `~/a/a/v2`, v1 secondary)

**The TUI starts a real HTTP server when asked to.** In v2
(`packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui.ts:233-249`):

```
const external = hasArg("--port") || hasArg("--hostname") || network.mdns === true
const transport = external
  ? { url: (await client.call("server", network)).url, ... }   // real HTTP listener
  : { url: "http://opencode.internal", fetch: createWorkerFetch(client), ... }  // in-process RPC only
```

So `opencode --mdns` (or `--port N` / `--hostname 0.0.0.0`) launches the TUI
**with a live HTTP API**. v1 has the identical mechanism
(`cli/tui/worker.ts` `server` RPC). `opencode serve` / `opencode web` start a
headless server the same way.

**mDNS** (`server/mdns.ts`): when enabled, publishes a service
`opencode-<port>`, type `http`, host `opencode.local` (override with
`--mdns-domain`), txt `{path:"/"}` via `bonjour-service`. Enabling `--mdns`
defaults the hostname to `0.0.0.0`.

**Flags + config** (`cli/network.ts`): `--port` (default 0 = prefer 4096 then
free), `--hostname`, `--mdns`, `--mdns-domain`, `--cors`. `serve`/`web` also
read `config.server.{port,hostname,mdns,mdnsDomain,cors}` from opencode.json.
(Note: the **TUI** path calls `resolveNetworkOptionsNoConfig` with no config,
so for the TUI these are **flag-only** today — a gotcha to document.)

**Endpoints that pin down the *active* session** (the whole point):
- `GET /session/status` → `{sessionID → {type: idle|busy|…}}`. Non-idle entries
  are the sessions actively running right now — a direct "active" signal the
  /proc heuristic cannot see. (`session/status.ts`: idle entries are dropped,
  so the map holds only busy sessions.)
- `GET /project/current` → the currently active project.
- `GET /session/{id}` and `/session/{id}/message` → full `SessionInfo` + message
  counts (feeds layer 8 of `cotail-session-report`).

## Deliverables

1. **Launch wrapper / docs** — a small script (e.g. an `oc-serve` shim or a
   documented alias) that starts `opencode --mdns` (v2; v1 fallback documented)
   so a server is always present. Record the gotchas (TUI = flag-only; set
   `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`; mDNS host `opencode.local`).
2. **mDNS discovery in cotails** — browse for `opencode-<port>`/`http` services
   to find running instances without a hardcoded port (a `bonjour-service`/mdns
   lookup, or scan the known 4096+ range as a fallback).
3. **HTTP resolver in `get-session`** — add an `--http <url>` / `--mdns` mode to
   `cotails get-session` that queries `/session/status` (+`/project/current`)
   for the active session, falling back to the existing `/proc` resolver when no
   server is found. This makes the resolver cross-platform and exact.
4. **Live fields** — pipe `/session/status` + message counts into the
   `SessionInfo` "live" layer (layer 8 of `cotail-session-report`).

## Direction across existing work

- **`cotail-get-session` (done)**: current `/proc` resolver becomes the offline
  fallback; HTTP becomes primary when a server is reachable.
- **`cotail-session-report`**: this ticket is the source of its layer-8 (live)
  fields — status, message count, last activity.
- **`cotail-history`**: could later annotate which sessions are live/busy.

## Acceptance

- A documented, scripted way to run opencode with HTTP+mDNS on (v2; v1 noted).
- `cotails get-session --mdns` (or `--http`) returns the *busy* session from a
  running instance, cross-platform.
- Falls back to `/proc` when no server/mDNS answer.
- Security note documented (auth/password, binding to localhost vs 0.0.0.0).

## Open questions

- Does opencode expose the TUI's *currently-selected* (viewed) session, or only
  *busy* ones, over HTTP? `TuiEvent.SessionSelect` is published on switch
  (`handlers/tui.ts`) — an event stream may be needed to track "viewed" vs
  "running". Confirm during implementation.

This is the preferred path; the shell alias (alias opencode='opencode --mdns') is only an interim workaround until that one-line upstream lands. Track in ~/src/doc/opencode-patches.md.

title: get-session: resolve active session ID from an opencode PID
description:
# `cotails get-session` — resolve the active session for a running opencode process

Given an opencode PID, return its **current active session id**. This is the first
command that answers "which session is *that* opencode instance on right now?",
and it lands the foundation for a consolidated **session-information report**.

## Inputs (PID resolution order)

1. **Positional arg** — `cotails get-session <pid>` (most explicit).
2. **`OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` env** — if already present (e.g. the
   `opencode-session-id-plugin` `shell.env` hook injected it into the tool
   shell cotails runs in), return it directly with no `/proc` or DB work.
3. **`OPENCODE_PID` env** — the opencode process PID (set by opencode itself
   on startup; inherited by every tool/subagent it spawns).

## PID → session mechanism (Linux `/proc`)

opencode does **not** write the active session to disk per-process, and a
TUI-mode process often runs **no HTTP listener** (so the server API is not a
reliable discovery path). The robust signal is:

1. Read `/proc/<pid>/cwd` → the project directory opencode is running in.
2. Read `/proc/<pid>/environ` → `OPENCODE_DB` (if set) to pick the right DB;
   otherwise auto-discover (`discoverDb`).
3. Query the `session` table for the **most recently `time_updated`** session
   whose `directory` matches that cwd.

This is version-agnostic: the `session` table (with `directory`,
`time_updated`) exists in **both** opencode v1 and v2 schemas, so the same
lookup serves `~/a/a/v2` (primary) and `~/a/a/v1` (legacy). The v1/v2 split
in cotails only matters for *content* (`part` vs `event` tables), not for
session metadata.

## Output / the session-information block

This ticket also introduces the canonical **`SessionInfo`** type — the start
of a standard session report that later tickets (`cotail-basic-fields`,
`cotail-fork-point`, `cotail-fork-time`) extend:

- `id`, `title`, `directory`, `slug`, `projectId`, `parentId`, `version`
- `timeCreated`, `timeUpdated` (epoch ms)

Output modes:
- default (human): session id prominent + key fields
- `--json`: full `SessionInfo` object (JSONL)
- `--id-only`: bare session id (scripting-friendly)

## Acceptance

- `cotails get-session` with no args resolves via `OPENCODE_PID`/`OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`.
- `cotails get-session <pid>` resolves via `/proc`.
- `--json` and `--id-only` modes work.
- Clear errors when: PID dead, not opencode-ish, no DB, no session for cwd.
- `SessionInfo` type + query live in `src/opencode/` for reuse.

title: Implement cotails history command
description:
Implement `cotails history` per `.design/history-viewer/design.md`.

## Behavior
- Filter: `session.time_updated >= now - since` (default `--since 24h`).
- Optional `--directory <path>` substring filter; optional `--limit <n>` (0 = unlimited).
- Per session emit: id, title, directory, messages_recent, messages_total, time_updated (plus slug/time_created in machine formats).
- Counts: sum `message` (v1) + `session_message` (v2) rows — they are mutually exclusive per session, so no mode detection is needed. In-window count uses `time_created >= cutoff`. Both hit the existing `(session_id, time_created, id)` indexes.
- Sort by `time_updated DESC`.

## Output
- default: human `table` (aligned, ANSI if TTY, truncate with ellipsis, footer count line).
- `--json`: JSONL, one object per line, ISO-8601 timestamps.
- `--tsv`: tab-separated with a header line, epoch-ms timestamps.
- `--json` wins if both `--json` and `--tsv` are passed.

## `--since` parsing
Accept `Nh` / `Nd` / `Nm` and absolute ISO-8601 / epoch-ms.

## Acceptance
- `cotails history` lists the ~100 sessions active in 24h on the live DB in under 200ms.
- `cotails history --json` and `--tsv` pipe cleanly.
- `--directory` and `--limit` filter correctly.
- Verified SQL is in the design doc.
notes: Done. 106 sessions in 24h at 81ms; --json/--tsv/--directory/--limit verified; recent vs total split correct; error paths exit 2.

description:
Restructure from a single flat `opencotails.ts` into a domain-grouped `src/` layout, give it one working entry point, a real installable `cotails` command, and subcommand dispatch. Project is <1.0, so breaking changes are fine.

## Naming / spelling (canonicalize)

- **Human action (flagged, not auto):** GitHub repo is `rektide/opencotails` (1t). Rename on GitHub to `opencoattails` and update the local remote URL.

## Target layout
```
src/
├── cli.ts                # ONE entry: shebang, main(), dispatch, top-level help
├── format.ts             # renderTable / emitJsonl / emitTsv + ANSI
├── opencode/             # abstractions · wrappers · types (version-agnostic)
│   ├── db.ts             #   discoverDb, openReadOnly, registerRegex
│   ├── types.ts          #   Session, MessageCounts, SearchHit, SearchTerms, HistoryFilter
```

A single DB can be mixed (v1-native + v2-native sessions during transition), so `Source` is **per-version** (`v1/` and `v2/` each implement it); `detectSources(db)` returns the set present. Commands iterate available sources and merge (history sums counts; search unions hits). - `cotails history` is recognized (stub ok).

- No `opencotails.ts` at root; no `index.js`/`opencotails.js` references remain.

title: Summary cache DB: store & reuse session summaries with full parameter capture
description:
# Summary cache DB — store & reuse session summaries

A cotail-owned database that persists agent summaries so they are reused
instead of regenerated (cost + latency). Mirrors the existing precedent of a
cotail-owned store: the planned FTS index at `~/.local/share/cotail/index.db`
(same "cotail owns it, separate from opencode's DB" pattern).

## Core requirement

**Capture the parameters of summarization so we know what got summarized how.**
A cache hit must mean "same session slice + same summarization configuration."
The cache key therefore includes:

- **content fingerprint** — hash of the actual selected part rows (preferred
  primary component, robust to rephrasing the flags while selecting the same
  content), AND
- the **selection scope** (flags + range that produced the slice), AND
- `agent`, `model`, `prompt_hash`.

Prefer the content fingerprint as the match signal so two different flag
combinations that select identical content still hit.

## Schema sketch

```sql
CREATE TABLE summary (
  session_id          TEXT NOT NULL,
  content_fingerprint TEXT NOT NULL,   -- hash of selected part rows
  scope               TEXT NOT NULL,   -- serialized selection flags/range
  agent               TEXT,
  model               TEXT,
  prompt_hash         TEXT NOT NULL,
  summary_text        TEXT NOT NULL,
  tokens              INTEGER,
  cost                REAL,
  source_version      TEXT,            -- v1 / v2
  created_at          INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (session_id, content_fingerprint, prompt_hash, model)
);
```

## Commands / tools

- **write** — `cotail cat --summarize --save` (or auto when cache enabled) writes summary + full params.
- **reuse** — on a later `--summarize`, consult the cache first; `--no-cache` bypasses; `--refresh` regenerates.
- **query** — `cotail summaries <sid>` lists cached summaries for a session with their params; `--json`.

## Parameters captured (per summary)

selection scope, content fingerprint, agent, model, prompt hash, source version
(v1/v2), tokens, cost, created_at — enough to know precisely what got
summarized and how.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** `cotail-summarize`.
- **Blocks on `cotail-cat-summarize`** — the `--summarize` flag defines the
  parameter shape this cache must store.

## Potential children (flesh out later)

- schema + capture (write path)
- lookup / reuse (read path, hit/miss, `--no-cache` / `--refresh`)
- `cotail summaries` query/list command

## Acceptance

- Summaries persist across runs; identical selection + config → cache hit, no agent call.
- Parameters fully captured (selection scope + content fingerprint + agent/model/prompt + tokens/cost + source version).
- `--no-cache` and `--refresh` work; `cotail summaries <sid>` lists cached summaries + params (`--json`).
- Cotail-owned DB; opencode's DB touched read-only.
acceptance_criteria: Summaries persist and are reused on identical selection+config (no agent call); full params captured (scope+fingerprint+agent/model/prompt+tokens/cost+source version); --no-cache/--refresh work; cotail summaries <sid> lists params; cotail-owned DB, opencode DB read-only.

description:
Synthesis view over file-use data: rank sessions by the share/count of file activity OUTSIDE session.directory. Surface "filed under A but most access is in B" candidates, inferring the likely target directory from the dominant external paths. Default threshold + override flag.

Depends on cotail-fileuse-tool.

Acceptance: a command lists sessions whose out-of-project file activity exceeds a threshold, with the inferred target directory.

title: Port cotails to Rust
description:
Rewrite cotails as a Rust project: the opencode source DB and the cotails FTS index read via the `turso` crate (or `rusqlite`), clap-v4 CLI, figment2 config, tracing. Rust is a natural fit for a fast local search/index tool and matches the broader toolchain.

Candidate scope:
- Read-only source-DB access (regex + display) reimplemented in Rust.
- Phase 1 FTS index (`cotail-index`) as a separate owned DB.
- Incremental indexing + `status`.

title: FTS index (Phase 1)
description: Build the cotail-owned full-text index as a consumer of the shared V2 query world. Index policy-approved cotail_document rows and source-qualified Targets without writing OpenCode's database. Support full and incremental indexing, explicit source/index generations, freshness and stale-session reporting, scoped runs by Session/directory/Project/time, and rebuild. Backend selection must preserve document identity, provenance, revisions, exposure policy, and live hydration/recheck semantics rather than depend on removed V1 part rows.
acceptance_criteria: cotail index and cotail status operate on a separate cotail-owned database; indexing consumes V2 logical documents and AccessPolicy rather than physical OpenCode tables; incremental checkpoints never equate Event watermarks with complete content history; source/index generation and staleness are explicit; Session/directory/Project/time scopes work; changed/deleted documents reconcile correctly; search results retain checked Targets, provenance, ranking/snippet/freshness, and authoritative live recheck; rebuild and interrupted-run recovery are tested.
notes: 2026-08-17: Rebased from the prototype V1 part/session.time_updated plan onto cotail_document, query Targets/revisions, AccessPolicy, and honest checkpoint semantics. Related to cotail-query-access-policy; hard epic-to-feature blocking edges are not supported by beads.
